title: Token-Free Hierarchical Indexing for RAG beyond LLM-based Summarization
claim: A three-stage system turns a corpus into a multi-perspective graph, consolidates it into a token-free hierarchy, and retrieves coarse-to-fine.
layout: 3 panels (two top, one wide bottom), left-to-right flow, tinted backgrounds per stage
description: The figure has three tinted panels. Panel (a), on a peach background, shows a Corpus icon splitting into Chunk1..ChunkN documents. Each chunk passes through a box labeled Semantic, Logic and Distance, which produces a Multi-Perspective Chunk Graph. That graph has weighted edges, with vol(α) and g(α) annotations on a circled community of nodes. Panel (b), on a green background, shows an arrow labeled SE minimization (Equation 2) leading to a 3D layered encoding tree. Chunk nodes sit on a lower plane and pentagon community nodes sit above, under a gray root. A zoomed inset shows child nodes v_i and v_1 with vectors h aggregated into a parent β (Equation 9). Panel (c), on a cyan background, shows a Query going through an LLM to become an Enhanced Query and a vector q. The vector is matched coarse-grained against the top-level tree, then fine-grained against lower nodes. The retrieved chunk and the Enhanced Query go into RAG, and the LLM produces an Answer marked with a green check.
caption: Overall framework of SeRAG.
abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) increasingly relies on hierarchical indexing, yet existing frameworks are bottlenecked by the high cost and information loss of recursive, LLM-based summarization. We propose SeRAG, a novel token-free hierarchical indexing framework that replaces textual summaries with an information-theoretic knowledge taxonomy. SeRAG first transforms a corpus into a multi-perspective graph capturing semantic, logical, and sequential dependencies, then minimizes structural entropy to induce a topologically-faithful encoding tree. To bridge the gap between abstract themes and granular facts, we introduce localized structural weight-based vector aggregation for token-free community consolidation. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SeRAG significantly reduces indexing overhead while outperforming state-of-the-art methods in complex multi-hop reasoning tasks.
